text:
maria: Heads-up — CI perf harness shows ~18% p99 increase on host-side request parsing after yesterday's ingress tweak. flamegraph uploaded: https://artifacts.redwood/pf/1744444444/flame.svg
perf-bot: deploy completed for branch ingress/stream-rewrite @1744444300 :white_check_mark:
aj: saw the graph. can you paste pprof top or callgraph? is the regression in tokenization, parsing, or network churn?
maria: top shows heavy time in parse_tokenize_and_coalesce -> writev -> http2_frame_assemble, plus some memcpy hotspots. attached the sample callstack.
sam: writev syscall count looks up. miniframeization changed recently — maybe frames are smaller but more frequent, causing syscalls to spike.
lee: we did flip serializer to the new edge-serializer variant in that PR; it shouldn't increase writev calls though. suspicious.
devon: repro locally with a small streaming workload: syscall per chunk went from ~1.1 -> ~2.0 avg. looks like the chunking logic retries on EAGAIN or does extra slicing.
maria: minimal repro we used:
```
for i in {1..10000}; do echo -n "msg$i" | nc -N localhost 8080; done
```
irina: fwiw KV cache eviction spikes align with the regression window — more parse churn => more ephemeral prefix keys and lower kv hit rate.
aj: can someone run pprof with --alloc_fraction=1 and grab top 20? also get per-syscall counts from strace on canary.
sam: also revisit batching hints: last week we changed min_batch_size to 1 for low-latency routes, that can disable coalescing heuristics. if coalescing is off, tiny writes will dominate.
lee: I'll add instrumentation to count writev calls per request in the next canary. we can detect if serializer switch coincided with the spike.
maria: opened rollback PR #1234. will auto-rollback if p99 > baseline threshold. tagging oncall.
perf-bot: Canary rollback armed by maria at 1744444477 :warning:
devon: short-term mitigation: add an in-host coalescer layer that buffers tiny write fragments up to a threshold before issuing writev. Drafting patch now.
irina: also request adding kv hit telemetry keyed by prefix-length and parse-path so we can correlate misses to parsing behavior.
aj: good plan. owners?
sam: my suggestion: lee -> kernel/writev telemetry + canary instrumentation, devon -> coalescer patch, irina -> kv telemetry, maria -> canary/rollback owner.
maria: agreed. I'll follow up with an incident blameless note and schedule a quick bisect session. thanks all.
